newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Economist Boiko gets Russian privatisation job.
newsitem.headline: Economist Boiko gets Russian privatisation job.

text.p: Maxim Boiko, propelled into the upper ranks of Russia's cabinet on Wednesday to take charge of privatisation, is a talented young economist who has years of experience working on the state sell-off programme.
Boiko, 37, was appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the State Property Committee -- Russia's privatisation minister -- to replace Alfred Kokh.
Like Kokh, who is moving to a career in the private sector, Boiko is an ally of economic policy chief Anatoly Chubais, and the change-over does not signal any policy change.
"My successor Maxim Boiko, a man of great professionalism, and I belong to the same team," Kokh said.
"He is a soldier of Chubais's party," said a Kremlin source.
Boiko, a thin, bespectacled intellectual, is currently deputy head of President Boris Yeltsin's administration, where he is in charge of relations with the regions.
He has a reputation as a tough administrator, and Kremlin sources said he could shake up the State Property Commitee staff.

He was brought into the Kremlin last August when Chubais became Yeltsin's chief of staff, and since March, when Chubais became one of two first deputy prime ministers, has served as a link between the administration and his mentor.

In the early 1990s he was an adviser to Chubais at the State Property Committee, and was one of the masterminds of the voucher privatisation programme, which gave millions of Russians shares in state-owned companies in what has been described as the world's biggest peacetime transfer of property.
From 1993 to 1996 he headed the Russian Privatisation Centre, an organisation funded by Western aid which promoted privatisation in Russia. Boiko published a book on the subject in 1995.
Under Boiko the privatisation centre managed an abortive attempt to sell off one quarter of telecoms holding company Svyazinvest in late 1995.
The deal, Russia's biggest privatisation, was won by Italian telecoms company Stet but subsequently fell through because of a disagreement over terms.
The stake was finally sold again last month to a Russian and foreign financial consortium.
Boiko was born on August 30, 1959. He is married with one son.
